rows.en: Touya: "...So this is my room..."
Yamato: "Ohhh, it's pretty nice, isn't it?
Oh, is this my bed?
Wow, it's so soft!"
Touya: "...You're like a little kid."
Yamato: "Hmph. That's better than having such a closed-off mind
you can't just express your happiness, isn't it?"
Touya: "It's just a place to sleep, isn't it? Anywhere's the same."
Yamato: "You only say that because you've got it so good.
If you don't realize it until you've lost it, it'll be too late."
Touya: "Yeah, yeah."
Yamato: "Sigh... Oh well. We've still got time
before we reach Belnea Fort. Let's explore the ship."
Yamato: "Sigh... Oh well. We've still got time
before we reach the Holy Land. Let's explore the ship."
Touya: "Nah. I'm tired, so I'm going to sleep."
Yamato: "Nooo! We're lucky everyone here
is so nice, but if you don't get to know them when you have the chance,
you'll end up all alone. Come on, up you get!"
Touya: "...Things were a little better
when you couldn't talk..."
Yamato: "...Did you say something?"
Touya: "Nothing! You want me to go suck up to everyone,
right?"
Yamato: "Nooo! I mean communication!"
Touya: "I know, I know. It was a joke."
Yamato: "Do you really understand?
Well, never mind. I'll give you a little lesson."
Touya: "Keep it short, please."
Yamato: "All right. Here goes."
Let the explanation go in one ear and out the other.
Listen properly.
Yamato: "...Ahem! Let's see. First, you need
to meet people. Nothing can happen if you don't."
Touya: "Huh? Isn't that obvious?"
Yamato: "Then do you know how to find them?
Do you know who's where?"
Touya: "How would I know? I'll just have to try rooms at random."
Yamato: "Hee hee hee... Well, I can tell you,
with my purrsonal sensor!
It lets me pinpoint everyone's whereabouts!"
Touya: "...What's this 'purrsonal sensor'?
I get that it's a personal sort of sensor, but..."
Yamato: "Heh. That... I don't really understand either."
Touya: "...Hey."
Yamato: "I-I'm joking, honestly. Um, it seems
to pick up specific people's brain waves.
That's how I can tell who's where in a flash.
The name I was given was more complicated,
but that's basically what it does, so I named it myself.
Well? Pretty cool feature, isn't it?"
Touya: "Well, it is useful.
Did Gabon install that too?"
Yamato: "That's right."
Touya: "...Honestly, that guy... He even put something like that in..."
Yamato: "It's useful, so what's the problem? Apparently
it was meant for emergencies. It seems to detect
when someone's brain waves differ from their registered pattern."
Touya: "What do you mean, when the pattern's different?"
Yamato: "Hmm... When emotions are running high, when someone's
in pain, or when they're thinking really hard about something..."
Touya: "So, when something unusual's happening?"
Yamato: "Exactly. Go see someone I've detected,
and there should be something going on.
Well, I can't promise there always will be."
Touya: "I see. Then let's get started..."
Yamato: "Stooop! I'm not finished yet.
There's one more important thing.
You can just chat normally, but sometimes you'll want
to discuss topics you've picked up along the way, right?"
Touya: "W-Well, yeah..."
Yamato: "When that happens, just press the Y button
and select 'Topic List.' It'll display the important information
you've collected so far.
Choose the subject you want to discuss,
then just talk to the person you have in mind."
Touya: "Huh... But that doesn't mean the person
will necessarily know about it, does it?"
Yamato: "Tsk, tsk, tsk.
You'll see for yourself, but each topic tells you
who it's meant for, so don't worry.
Someone's name appears in '( )'
after the subject, and your chosen topic is displayed too.
That's all taken care of."
Touya: "Then I guess I don't need to worry..."
Yamato: "Oh, right. About those topics...
You can't choose them as many times as you like."
Touya: "...What do you mean?"
Yamato: "There's a number called Topic Points.
When you select a topic and talk to that person,
it goes down by one.
Once it reaches zero, you can't choose any more.
So you need to think about what you choose,
rather than just trying everything at random."
Touya: "Sounds like a hassle."
Yamato: "Don't say that.
The world's not so kind that you can get through
everything by winging it."
Touya: "Yeah, yeah."
Yamato: "Hmm, what else do I need
to explain...? 'Move,' I guess."
Touya: "What's that?"
Yamato: "It's a system for going straight to a specific place
when walking around the map gets tedious.
Select it, and you'll see the names
of various places inside Liebhofen.
Choose one, and you can go there instantly.
It's a handy feature. But until you get used to the ship,
you should walk around yourself.
If you use it too much,
you'll lose track of where you are.
Each floor of Liebhofen has a simple layout,
but there are five of them, so don't get careless."
Touya: "Yeah, you're right."
Yamato: "Good, you're listening. And finally,
when you've had enough, select 'Finish.'
That ends this phase."
Touya: "Okay."
Yamato: "That was brief, but that's the end of the explanation.
Now the best way to learn is to try it yourself."
Yeah, I get it. Let's go.
Could you explain it again?
Yamato: "Ohhh!"
Touya: "W-What?"
Yamato: "I forgot something important.
When you talk to everyone, you can get closer to them,
and they may start to like you.
You can also check how things stand
with them right now. With another of my features, of course."
Touya: "...They really put all sorts of stuff in you, didn't they?"
Yamato: "Well, I'm still me.
Anyway, when you want to know, select 'Yamato's Check,'
and you'll find out everyone's feelings in a flash!"
Touya: "Y-Yeah... I'll make good use of it."
Yamato: "...And that's how it works. Got it?"
Touya: "All right, let's go."
Yamato: "Hey, did you really understand?!"
Touya: "It's fine. Come on, let's go."

review_batches.context: Read full138-row tutorial. Yamato enjoys the room, urges Touya to meet others; Belnea Fort/Holy Land destination alternatives precede listen/skip choices and personal-sensor/topic explanation.
review_batches.decisions: Keep destination variants separate, cyborg-cat identity and Gabon's fictional feature explanation attributed. Purrsonal reproduces cat pronunciation as accepted variant of personal sensor. Preserve no-guarantee event caveat, exact Dreamcast Y button and select-topic-then-speak sequence. Topic List matches English UI rather than source's shortened Topic wording.
